stories.headline: FIIs step up India buying, pour Rs 13,750 crore on Friday; total buying hits Rs 53,154 crore in 14 days
stories.title: FIIs step up India buying, pour Rs 13,750 crore on Friday; total buying hits Rs 53,154 crore in 14 days

With the latest purchase, cumulative FII investments since October 16 have reached Rs 53,154 crore, according to the exchange data.Friday's buying followed another massive investment of Rs 14,975 crore on Thursday, November 5, marking the biggest single-day FII purchase in Indian equities in more than a year.The pace of foreign buying has accelerated in recent sessions, with FIIs investing a net Rs 34,584 crore over the past five trading sessions alone. The latest inflows mark a sharp turnaround from the prolonged selling witnessed earlier this year, when overseas investors withdrew billions of dollars from Indian equities.The foreign buying came even as domestic institutional investors (DIIs) continued to sell. DIIs offloaded shares worth a net Rs 5,969 crore on Friday, following net sales of Rs 10,445 crore in the previous session. Their combined net selling over the two sessions stood at Rs 16,414 crore.The return of foreign buying follows months of sustained selling amid elevated crude oil prices, geopolitical tensions in West Asia, a weakening rupee and concerns over corporate earnings.Foreign selling intensified in September and October as oil prices climbed and global investors reduced their exposure to emerging markets. The outflows had pushed foreign ownership of Indian equities to historic lows.Global brokerage Nomura said Indian equities could become more attractive to foreign investors as earnings improve and valuations remain below their post-pandemic averages. opening: Foreign institutional investors (FIIs) stepped up their buying in Indian equities on Friday, November 6, pumping in a net Rs 13,750 crore and extending their buying streak to 14 trading sessions.
With the latest purchase, cumulative FII investments since October 16 have reached Rs 53,154 crore, according to the exchange data.
body: Friday's buying followed another massive investment of Rs 14,975 crore on Thursday, November 5, marking the biggest single-day FII purchase in Indian equities in more than a year.
The pace of foreign buying has accelerated in recent sessions, with FIIs investing a net Rs 34,584 crore over the past five trading sessions alone.
The latest inflows mark a sharp turnaround from the prolonged selling witnessed earlier this year, when overseas investors withdrew billions of dollars from Indian equities.
The foreign buying came even as domestic institutional investors (DIIs) continued to sell.
DIIs offloaded shares worth a net Rs 5,969 crore on Friday, following net sales of Rs 10,445 crore in the previous session.
Their combined net selling over the two sessions stood at Rs 16,414 crore.
The return of foreign buying follows months of sustained selling amid elevated crude oil prices, geopolitical tensions in West Asia, a weakening rupee and concerns over corporate earnings.
Foreign selling intensified in September and October as oil prices climbed and global investors reduced their exposure to emerging markets.
The outflows had pushed foreign ownership of Indian equities to historic lows.
Global brokerage Nomura said Indian equities could become more attractive to foreign investors as earnings improve and valuations remain below their post-pandemic averages.
It also noted that the correction in artificial intelligence-related stocks in international markets could encourage investors to redirect capital towards other markets, including India.
Expectations of a possible reduction in long-term capital gains tax for foreign investors have also added to optimism, although any such change remains uncertain.

Why FIIs are suddenly shopping Indian stocks non-stop this DiwaliSensex, Nifty climb higherIndian equities defied a global sell-off on Friday, extending their winning streak as investors turned to domestic markets as a relative safe haven amid turmoil across global markets.
The Nifty 50 surged 494 points, or 2.01%, to settle at 25,030, while the BSE Sensex advanced 1,718 points, or 2.17%, to close at 81,028.
The broader markets, however, came under pressure.
The Nifty Smallcap 250 declined 0.85%, while the Nifty Midcap 100 ended marginally lower, signalling continued weakness beyond the benchmark indices.
The Nifty Consumer Durables index also gained around 2%.
Despite the sharp gains in benchmark indices, market volatility remained elevated.
The India VIX, which gauges expected market volatility, surged more than 13% to trade near the 18 mark.

stories.headline: Congress vows to continue fight against ‘vote chori’
stories.title: Congress vows to continue fight against ‘vote chori’
stories.summary: Akhnoor, Nov 06: JKPCC president Tariq Hameed Karra has asserted that the Congress would continue its fight to ensure free and fair elections and safeguard every citizen’s right to vote, saying the party would not allow any attempt to undermine democracy in the country. Addressing a Congress gathering at Akhnoor on Friday, organised by newly appointed Chairman of the JKPCC Scheduled Caste Department, Ashok Bhagat, Karra said the efforts of Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi had exposed various alleged modes of “vote chori” by the BJP-led government through Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. He claimed that more than 13 crore people had been deprived of their right to vote so far and alleged that the Modi government had indulged in large-scale electoral manipulation over the past several years, which had now been brought to light. Karra said the right to vote was the most precious right of every citizen in a democracy, but alleged that the BJP was attempting to take it away. He asserted that the Congress and like-minded forces would not allow such practices to continue. Referring to the recent rally against “vote chori” in Delhi, he said it had reflected the mood of people across the country. He urged party workers to continue exposing what he described as the BJP’s attempts to take away the rights of ordinary citizens. Karra said restoration of statehood remained the main agenda of the J&K Congress, alleging that the BJP had taken away the statehood status of Jammu and Kashmir along with other significant rights of its people. He said people were suffering in the absence of statehood. Congratulating Ashok Bhagat on his appointment, Karra recalled his contribution during the Assembly elections and said he had been elevated in the party to represent the voice of the downtrodden and oppressed sections of society. He said Bhagat’s academic knowledge and administrative experience had also been considered while assigning him the responsibility. JKPCC Working President Raman Bhalla, while addressing the gathering, raised the issue of the proposed railway connectivity project to Rajouri-Poonch via Akhnoor and Sunderbani, which has been awaiting clearance for more than 13 years. Questioning the BJP’s stand on the project, Bhalla criticised the delay and said the failure to take up the important railway link had ignored the needs of a vast area, particularly the border belt. He described Ashok Bhagat as an intelligent and hardworking leader with strong grassroots connections and praised the PCC president and the Congress high command for selecting the right person for the position. Bhalla also said people were caught between two power centres in the absence of statehood and asserted that the Congress would not rest until statehood was restored to Jammu and Kashmir. Former minister Mula Ram criticised the BJP, alleging that its policies had deprived poor and downtrodden sections of their rights while subjecting people to unprecedented price rise and unemployment. He also accused the party of electoral manipulation, saying the poor and the youth were suffering under the present regime.

stories.headline: Supreme Court decision on BBMB arrears a victory for Himachal, says CM Sukhu
stories.title: Supreme Court decision on BBMB arrears a victory for Himachal, says CM Sukhu
stories.summary: The order settles a decades-old dispute over Himachal Pradesh’s 7.19% share in the power generated from the projects
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: Himachal Pradesh Chief Minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu on Friday (November 6, 2026) termed the Supreme Court’s decision directing Punjab and Haryana to supply 11,973 million units of electricity to the State over 20 years towards its outstanding dues from the Bhakra-Nangal and Beas hydroelectric projects a historic victory for its people.
The order settles a decades-old dispute over Himachal Pradesh’s 7.19% share in the power generated from the projects.

The State will receive nearly 60 crore units annually during the lean season, generating an estimated revenue of ₹10,000 crore to ₹20,000 crore over the 20-year period, depending on electricity prices, Mr. Sukhu said in a statement.
He said the decision could fetch the State additional revenue of up to ₹1,000 crore annually.
Even at ₹6 per unit, Himachal Pradesh would earn at least ₹500 crore a year, while a rate of ₹13-14 per unit would significantly increase the returns.
Mr. Sukhu attributed the outcome to the State government’s sustained legal battle and determination to secure its financial rights.
He described it as the fourth major success in protecting Himachal Pradesh’s interests, citing earlier victories in matters relating to Wildflower Hall, the Kishau Dam among others.
The Chief Minister said the government was also pursuing its claims over the Shanan Power Project and the water cess.

The additional revenue, he said, would be used to strengthen education and healthcare, improve road infrastructure, generate employment and ensure timely payment of financial benefits to government employees.
Congratulating the State’s nearly 75 lakh residents, Mr. Sukhu said protecting its resources and making Himachal Pradesh self-reliant remained a top priority for his government.

stories.headline: Supreme Court Orders SIT Probe Into Illegal Gravel Mining In Rajasthan's Luni, Jojari And Bandi Rivers, Bars New Industries Near River Ecosystem
stories.title: Supreme Court Orders SIT Probe Into Illegal Gravel Mining In Rajasthan's Luni, Jojari And Bandi Rivers, Bars New Industries Near River Ecosystem
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court has directed the Rajasthan government to constitute a Special Investigation Team (SIT) within three days to investigate organised illegal bajri (gravel) mining in the Luni, Jojari and Bandi rivers and their tributaries, including the involvement of public officials in facilitating such activities.

A bench of Justice Vikram Nath and Justice Sandeep Mehta, in an order dated October 26, also restrained the State from granting permissions for the establishment of new industrial units along or in the vicinity of the riverine ecosystem until the High Flood Line and buffer zones are scientifically determined.
The SIT, to be headed by an officer not below the rank of Inspector General of Police, will include the Superintendents of Police of Jodhpur, Balotra and Pali.
“The SIT shall undertake a comprehensive investigation into organised illegal bajri mining activities affecting the Luni, Jojari and Bandi rivers and their tributaries.

The investigation shall extend to identifying the persons and entities involved in such activities, the networks through which the illegal extraction, transportation and sale of bajri are organised, and the beneficiaries of such operations”, the Court ordered.
The SIT also has to examine whether public officials facilitated or enabled illegal mining, including instances of collusion, dereliction of duty or failure to act despite knowledge of violations.
Appropriate action has to be initiated against those found responsible.
The Court directed the SIT to file a status report before it on or before the next date of hearing on 27th November, 2026.
The Court directed that an additional protective zone of 100 metres be maintained on either side of the respective recorded outer boundaries of the rivers.
The Court held that No Red Category industry shall be permitted to be established within a distance of 500 metres from the said recorded outer boundaries.

Observing that the issues involved in the present proceedings are complex and multifaceted in nature, the Court appointed Senior Advocate Balbir Singh along with Advocate on Record Namit Saxena as Amici Curiae to assist the Court in the effective consideration and resolution of the issues.

The Court passed the directions in the suo motu proceedings concerning pollution in the Jojari-Luni-Bandi river system, which has affected the environment and the lives of approximately 20 lakh people.

stories.headline: Supreme Court Dismisses Plea Challenging Allahabad HC's Senior Designations Conferred In 2019
stories.title: Supreme Court Dismisses Plea Challenging Allahabad HC's Senior Designations Conferred In 2019
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Friday (November 6) dismissed a plea challenging senior advocate designations conferred by the Allahabad High Court in 2019.
A bench of Justice PS Narasimha and Justice Alok Aradhe observed that the applicants who were not conferred the designation could apply afresh in the next round.
Advocate Pranav Sachdeva for the petitioner submitted that the petitioner was not considered despite having 15 years of unblemished continuous practice in Allahabad High Court.
However, Justice Narashimha questioned why he wanted to litigate the issue, responding, "Apply.
Why do you want to litigate?
You apply afresh.
Don't unnecessarily litigate."
Sachdeva alleged that the selection committee has not done the evaluation for several years despite the judgment in Jitendra Kalla.
State of NCT holding that at least one exercise of senior designation must be done every calendar year.
Ultimately, the Court ordered, "We are not inclined to interfere with the order passed by the High Court.

We make it clear that the petitioner will be entitled to reapply and upon such application it shall be considered in accordance with the law that governs the subject, including the principle laid down in Jitendra Kalla's case."
The Special Leave Petition was filed against the September 2024 judgment of the Allahabad High Court which rejected the petition filed by Advocate Vishnu Bihari Tiwari against the 2019 designations.
